t: The Signature Bin System: One Family, Total Interop
title: The Signature Bin System: One Family, Total Interop
description: The Signature bin system is Justin Addam Higgins' one-family organizer: bins, grid boxes, and trays sharing one footprint and one rail standard — every container stacks, hangs, and carts together. Buy any Signature container and it fits every Signature mount. The interop is the product: organization that never hits a compatibility wall.

demo.program:
print("ONE footprint + ONE rail: bins, grid boxes, trays all interoperate.")
print("Stacks, hangs, carts: every container fits every mount.")
print("Interop IS the product: never a compatibility wall.")

t: Signature Bin With Built-In Kanban Window
title: Signature Bin With Built-In Kanban Window
description: Each Signature bin has a kanban window on its front — a slot holding the reorder card, visible without opening or moving the bin. Stock hits the card line, card flips red, the wall signals restock at a glance. The inventory thinking is molded into the bin instead of taped on as an afterthought.

demo.program:
print("Kanban window on bin front: reorder card visible, no moving bins.")
print("Stock hits line -> card flips RED: wall signals restock at a glance.")
print("Inventory thinking MOLDED IN, not taped on.")

title: Signature Color-Family System
description: Signature bins come in the category colors — blue fasteners, red electrical, green cooling, yellow consumables — molded through, never painted. The wall reads as a color map: low blue means order screws, empty red means order cables. Color plus label gives two find paths, and stock status reads from across the room.

demo.program:
print("Molded colors: blue fasteners, red electrical, green cooling, yellow consumables.")
print("Wall = color map: low blue -> order screws. Two find paths: color + label.")
print("Stock status readable from across the room.")

print("Reconfigure in seconds. Grid = dividers that WORK, not annoy.")

title: Signature vs Standard Bin Systems
description: Standard: bins from three brands that don't stack, labels taped on, kanban in a spreadsheet somewhere. Signature: one family, molded kanban windows, color categories, locking dividers, powered panel option. Same polypropylene — the Signature adds the system thinking that makes bins a library instead of a pile of boxes.

demo.program:
print("Standard: mixed brands, taped labels, spreadsheet kanban.")
print("Signature: one family, kanban windows, color map, locking dividers, power option.")
print("Same plastic. System thinking: library, not pile of boxes.")

title: Signature Mobile Cart Integration
description: The Signature cart takes the same bins off the same wall — lift, hang on cart, roll. The cart's rails match the wall's exactly, so transfer is seconds and labels stay facing out. The job-site library is the wall library, relocated. Return is the reverse: hang back, done.

demo.program:
print("Cart rails == wall rails: lift bins off wall, hang on cart, roll.")
print("Seconds to transfer, labels stay out. Job site = wall, relocated.")
print("Return: hang back. Done.")

print("Segments match teardown flows. One motion, not two locations.")
print("Staging + filing: unified at the wall.")

title: Signature Inventory App Pairing
description: The Signature bins pair with a simple inventory app: scan the bin's barcode, adjust count, and the app tracks stock against kanban minimums — alerting before stockouts. The physical kanban cards remain the primary signal; the app is the backup and the ordering history. Physical first, digital second.

demo.program:
print("Scan barcode -> adjust count -> app tracks vs minimums, alerts pre-stockout.")
print("Physical cards = primary signal. App = backup + history.")
print("Physical first, digital second: the right priority.")
